decisive_items: cyanosis of fingers and toes progressed to well-demarcated gangrene below the elbows and knees
contrast angiogram of the aorta and its branches showed patent thoracic and abdominal aorta and no filling defects in major limb arteries
Ecchymoses were present over the extremities, and he bled easily from puncture sites
response.rationale: Progressive distal gangrene with patent large arteries in the setting of sepsis and DIC indicates microvascular thrombosis, characteristic of purpura fulminans rather than sepsis or DIC alone.

rejected.why: Sepsis is the underlying trigger but does not explain the progressive gangrene with patent large arteries.
DIC is a complication present in this case, but the specific clinical picture of ecchymoses and gangrene with patent major arteries is purpura fulminans.
